metaData.originalTitle: 未来五年，比技术更值钱的是这些基础能力
metaData.title: In the Next Five Years, These Foundational Skills Will Be More Valuable Than Technical Skills
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: Based on a large-scale study covering 70 million job transitions, this article demonstrates that in an era of shrinking technology half-lives, foundational skills such as collaboration, mathematical thinking, and adaptability are more decisive of long-term career ceilings and organizational adaptability than specialized technical skills.
metaData.summary: Based on large-scale data from over 70 million job transitions across more than 1,000 occupations in the United States between 2005 and 2019, the article categorizes skills into foundational skills (reading comprehension, basic math, teamwork) and specialized advanced skills (such as blockchain). The study finds that individuals with higher foundational skill scores earn higher wages throughout their careers, get promoted faster, learn new skills more quickly, and adapt better to industry changes. As the half-life of technical skills shrinks from 10 years to 4 years and may drop below 2 years, the importance of foundational skills becomes increasingly prominent. Social skills (communication, empathy, conflict resolution) in particular serve as the glue for efficient team collaboration, and the proportion of management job postings emphasizing collaboration, coaching, and influence has tripled since 2007. The article provides three specific recommendations for leaders: prioritize screening candidates with strong foundational skills during hiring; invest in early-career development to strengthen soft skills; and have managers lead by example to model and reward foundational skill behaviors.

mainPoints.point: Foundational skills (collaboration, mathematical thinking, adaptability) determine long-term career ceilings more than specialized technical skills.
mainPoints.explanation: The study finds that individuals with higher foundational skill scores get promoted faster, learn new skills more efficiently, and adapt better to industry changes, while specialized technical skills become obsolete at an accelerating pace.

mainPoints.point: Social skills are the glue for efficient team collaboration, and the related demand continues to grow.
mainPoints.explanation: Since 2007, the proportion of management job descriptions emphasizing collaboration, coaching, and influence has tripled; jobs combining cognitive abilities with social skills command the highest wage premiums.

mainPoints.point: Enterprises should prioritize foundational skills in hiring and development, rather than focusing solely on specialized knowledge.
mainPoints.explanation: It is recommended to assess candidates' learning ability, collaboration, and response to uncertainty through targeted questions during hiring; and to invest resources in early-career development to strengthen communication, collaboration, and learning agility.

mainPoints.point: Managers can reinforce foundational skills through daily behavioral modeling and system design.
mainPoints.explanation: Integrate soft skill development into team culture using tools such as peer feedback, mentoring, and team retrospectives, and recognize and reward thoughtful communication and collaborative problem-solving.

keyQuotes: In an era when technical expertise can become obsolete in just a few years, foundational skills are more important than ever.

Researchers estimate that the 'half-life' of technical skills—the time it takes for half of your acquired knowledge to become outdated—has shrunk from about 10 years in the 1980s to just 4 years today, and could soon shrink to less than 2 years.

relatedArticles.title: The Only Person Who Deeply Participated in Both ByteDance and Meituan's Organizational Building | Talking with AI Entrepreneur Wei Xiaokang
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: An in-depth conversation with Wei Xiaokang, the only person who has deeply participated in the organizational development of both ByteDance and Meituan, dissecting the underlying logic of organization and recruitment at top internet companies, and exploring the transformation of organizational forms and talent strategies for startups in the AI era.

relatedArticles.title: "Pessimists Are Right, Optimists Succeed": Chatting with Friend Yating about the AI Industry
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Veteran investor Zhuang Minghao starts from the fundamental logic of VC, deeply deconstructing the startup paradigms under the AI wave, the endgame of model competition, and the ultimate questioning of human career and existential value.

relatedArticles.title: 101 A Complaint-Free World | People Addicted to Complaining Have Already Written a Script of Failure for Themselves
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: An in-depth analysis of the book "The Complaint-Free World". The two hosts use personal anecdotes and psychological insights to reveal how complaining becomes addictive and turns people into "victims", and share actionable guidance to quit hidden complaining and reshape life from a builder's perspective.

relatedArticles.title: AI Replaces Newcomers: Cost Reduction or a Hidden Risk?
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: From the perspectives of organizational strategy and social responsibility, this article argues that companies should not massively eliminate entry-level jobs due to AI. Instead, they should redesign these roles to cultivate future leaders, spark innovation, enrich culture, and maintain social stability.

relatedArticles.title: Investing in AI with No Returns? Over 1,000 Global Executives Provide the Definitive Answer
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Based on a survey of over 1,000 global executives, this article reveals seven key factors for enterprises to realize AI economic value and proposes a six-stage model for measuring AI investment maturity, emphasizing that the core of AI success lies in management rather than technology.

relatedArticles.title: Vol.83 The Gourmand and the 'Cocoon'
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Starting from Suzhou's Pingtan storytelling and local cuisine, Xu Zhiyuan shares his personal shift from obsessively searching for life's meaning to embracing life's interestingness, and explores how OWSPACE bookstore is localizing and integrating with Suzhou's culture in a new journey.

relatedArticles.title: Which Jobs Are Growing, and Which Are Disappearing? The Data Has the Answer
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Based on actual employment data from S&P 500 companies, this article reveals five cross-industry trends in the AI-era job structure: expansion of physical execution roles, infrastructure-ization of software engineering capabilities, restructuring of sales systems, contraction of middle management, and the diffusion of AI roles into traditional industries. It predicts that organizational structures will evolve from a pyramid to a dumbbell shape.

relatedArticles.title: 14. Jane Eyre: How Far Must a Woman Who Is Neither Beautiful, Rich, Nor Lovable Go to Be Seen?
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Jiang Fangzhou provides a deep analysis of 'Jane Eyre' and the legendary life of its author, Charlotte Brontë, exploring how women can reclaim their sense of self through reflection and independence, moving from 'invisibility' to being 'seen.'

relatedArticles.title: What Kind of Leadership Do Enterprises Need in the Era of Agentic AI?
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article explores how enterprises can transition from simple AI automation to the era of Agentic AI, proposing leadership transformation strategies across four dimensions: governance, risk control, organizational structure, and culture.

relatedArticles.title: Organizations Over-reliant on AI Are Losing Three Core Capabilities
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article explores the risks of organizational over-reliance on AI—specifically the atrophy of employee thinking, the black-boxing of decision-making, and the erosion of social capital—and proposes practical strategies to strengthen competitiveness by preserving human judgment and deliberative structures.
